prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Pruning tips? Organic basil plant I purchased May 2019

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
The plant is healthy. It has become woody and leggy from years of pruning above bare stem instead of at a leaf node. Basil stems harden with age, and a bare woody stalk will not regrow leaves well, so it is now just taking energy from the plant. Your leafy side growth and the seedlings are the productive parts.

**Fix:**

1. **Cut the bare woody stalk.** Remove it at the base, or back to the lowest pair of leaves on it, using clean scissors. Don't leave a bare stub.
2. **Pinch, don't chop.** Cut just above a pair of leaves, where two new shoots will branch. Each cut should leave at least two sets of leaves on the stem. Never remove more than about a third of the plant at once.
3. **Remove flower buds** as soon as you see them. Flowering signals the plant to stop making leaves, and it is the main reason basil gets woody.
4. **Give it bright light and water when the top inch of soil is dry.** The recent repot is fine, and the seedlings show the roots are established. Once the new seedlings are a few inches tall, thin them so the strongest one or two remain.

Also, basil is an annual or short-lived plant, so even well-pruned plants usually decline after a year or two. If the leaves get smaller or the plant keeps going woody, replacing it with a fresh plant grown from one of these seedlings is the best long-term plan.
